name: tr_rj
caption:
IF RJ HAD A POKÉMON TEAM, HERE'S WHO WE'D SEND OUT 🎮🏀

🦖 Tyrunt: the Royal Heir Pokémon. Born right here in Toronto
🐍 Seviper: a snake that sharpens its bladed tail for battle. The Maple Mamba, nicknamed for playing like Kobe
🥉 Bronzong: the Bronze Bell Pokémon. Sealed Canada's World Cup bronze over the USA
🐦 Dodrio: three heads, three brains. 25 points, 10 rebounds, 15 assists
🔥 Magmortar: blasts fireballs from the ends of its arms. Playoff career-high 33 points vs Cleveland
🐉 Salamence: wished for wings so hard, it grew them. Our scorer, 21.6 points a night through 9 games

That's a party we'd take into any building. Which one would you swap in? 👇

Monster sprites: PMD Sprite Collab (sprites.pmdcollab.org), CC BY-NC 4.0

beats.vo: If RJ Barrett had a Pokemon team, here's what we'd be running.
beats.dlg: IF RJ HAD A TEAM|OF MONSTERS...

beats.vo: First up, Tyrunt. Its species is literally the Royal Heir Pokemon. Born right here in Toronto. A baby raptor.
beats.dlg: THE ROYAL HEIR POKEMON.|BORN IN TORONTO!

beats.vo: Seviper. A snake that sharpens its bladed tail on rocks for battle. The Maple Mamba, a nickname from playing like Kobe.
beats.dlg: SNAKE WITH A BLADED TAIL.|MAPLE MAMBA: LIKE KOBE!

beats.vo: Bronzong. The Bronze Bell Pokemon. For Canada, he sealed a bronze medal win over the United States.
beats.dlg: THE BRONZE BELL POKEMON.|BRONZE OVER THE USA!

beats.vo: Dodrio. Three heads, three brains. Twenty-five points, ten boards, fifteen assists.
Magmortar. It blasts fireballs from the ends of its arms. Thirty-three points in a playoff game against Cleveland.
beats.dlg: IT BLASTS FIREBALLS.|33 IN A PLAYOFF GAME!

beats.vo: And the ace. Salamence. It wanted wings so badly, it grew them. Our scorer, twenty-one point six a night through nine games.
beats.dlg: WANTED WINGS. GREW THEM.|21.6 A NIGHT, 9 GAMES IN!

beats.vo: That's a party we'd take into any building. Which one would you swap in? Comment below.
beats.dlg: A PARTY WE'D TAKE INTO|ANY BUILDING. WHO'S IN?

facts.claim: Barrett was born in Toronto; nicknamed the Maple Mamba due to his playstyle resemblance to Kobe Bryant; sealed Canada's victory over the United States with a 3 point shot to win bronze at the 2023 FIBA World Cup; first career triple-double: 25 points, 10 rebounds and 15 assists (November 16, 2024); April 24, 2026, Game 3 vs Cleveland: playoff career-high 33 points; selected third overall (#3) in the 2019 draft
